findings.title: Registry coverage and deep product coverage measure different things
findings.text: The original 85 adapter rows, 5,688 symbol candidates and five deep carry chapters do not establish whole-market product completeness. This expansion adds ten selected families and preserves registry identities, while T capital and historical return coverage remain separate.

findings.title: Expired ETH principal-token markets belong in the historical universe
findings.text: The captured official Ethereum registry has 494 unique markets, 117 ETH-tagged markets and 4 ETH-tagged active, unexpired markets at the 4 October discovery. Historical entries preserve maturities and identities, not historical peak capital.

findings.title: PT-stETH is denominated in stETH despite a wstETH feed label
findings.text: The December 2027 market identifies stETH as its accounting unit while wstETH is the underlying token. A one-unit maturity payoff is not automatically one wstETH. The feed reports the same market liquidity for the PT-buy and LP rows, so summing them would duplicate capital.

findings.title: Published PT looping is not proof of current ETH PT loops
findings.text: The official Ethereum looping catalog contains 15 PT identities. None matches an ETH-tagged market in the full captured registry. These published routes are USD families. ETH loops elsewhere require their own contract and borrowing evidence.

findings.title: Base APY is a feed classification, not audited organic cash
findings.text: The K3 Monad WETH row reports 2.69201% total APY, including 1.20737% base and 1.48464% rewards. autoETH reports 2.65708% total, including 2.47077% base and 0.18631% rewards. Incentives-off comparisons retain the distinction between quoted estimates and realized net returns.

findings.title: A perpetual LP earns a total trading payoff, not only a fee yield
findings.text: GM token value includes net trader PnL and inventory price exposure. The ETH index does not determine the collateral denomination: ETH-USDC, ETH-ETH and USDG-USDG markets have different capital exposure. A hedge is a separate position and is not verified by the GM wrapper itself.

findings.title: A current yield list hides retired and impaired products
findings.text: The official Yearn interface identifies yETH as retired and recovery-only. Resolv documents a March 2026 incident and recovery process. These are different failure cases, with different eligibility and cash rights; neither can be represented by an ordinary current APY.

findings.title: ETH options have proven historical capacity; current capacity still needs proof
findings.text: Ribbon documented a full 10,000 ETH call cap during its 2021 incentive program. Thetanuts publishes ETH call contract identities across Ethereum, Arbitrum and Mantle. The latter catalog alone does not establish active auctions, balances or material current ETH capacity.

findings.title: Listed and custodial staking can be large without adding a new payer
findings.text: WBETH and staking ETFs ultimately earn Ethereum validator rewards. Their distinctive risks lie in custody, charges, share pricing and exit access. Receipt layers and the ETH backing must be netted before combining them with onchain products.

families.returnBasis: Complete return is pool inventory price change plus the LP share of fees and net trader PnL, less execution costs. Funding transfers between opposing trader sides are not automatically LP income. A separate short hedge adds funding, collateral and liquidation costs.
families.exitTerms: Deposits and withdrawals execute through oracle/keeper steps. Open-interest reserves can restrict withdrawal capacity; liquidity must be released before all shares can exit.

families.incentivesOff: Fees and net counterparty trading results remain when emissions stop. A fee-only APY omits the largest sources of positive or negative total return.
families.coverageStatus: Official Arbitrum market catalog and material GM pool identities captured. Historical holdings, NAV plus distributions and any actual hedge are not reconstructed.

families.name: ETH options and structured vaults
families.mechanic: A covered-call vault sells calls against ETH collateral. Option buyers pay premium in exchange for upside above the strike. Cash-secured puts instead start with dollar collateral and sell ETH downside protection. Wheel products rotate between these exposures.
payers: Option buyers paying insurance or speculative premia
Reward-token sponsors where enabled

families.ETHexposure: Covered calls are ETH long with capped upside. Cash-secured ETH puts are USD-funded short downside exposure, not ordinary ETH staking.
families.returnBasis: Covered-call total return includes premium, the short-option settlement and ETH collateral movement, less fees. ETH-relative performance can be negative in a sharp rally. Cash-secured put return includes settlement losses. Annualizing auction premium alone is not realized net return.
families.exitTerms: Option collateral is committed until the round settles. Ribbon withdrawal requests are completed after rollover; unused pending deposits can use a separate instant withdrawal path. Secondary exits depend on the specific wrapper and liquidity.
families.controls: Ribbon historical docs list a 2% annual management fee and 10% performance fee, charged only for profitable strategy weeks. Keeper/manager roles select or roll options and auction parameters; T authority and current operations are not established.
families.capacity: Option buyer appetite, executable strike liquidity and risk limits. Larger vaults can depress auction premiums. Weekly caps and auction fills are real capacity measures.
families.incentivesOff: Option premiums can remain without RBN or NUTS incentives, but premium alone is not profit. The 2021 Ribbon period was explicitly incentivized, so the historical growth does not establish unsubsidized demand.
families.coverageStatus: Historical material ETH covered calls verified. Thetanuts official ETH contract identities are discovery only; no current $5 million ETH option-vault balance is established.

families.exitTerms: sUSDe unstaking returns USDe after its documented cooldown, not ETH. Rewards are discretionary under the current Ethena mechanism. families.capacity: Exchange risk limits, available open interest, collateral liquidity and basis demand. Market size does not imply an ETH-only neutral strategy can absorb all that capital.
families.incentivesOff: Actual funding and collateral income can remain without token rewards, but they are cyclical. Sustainable yield requires realized positive net carry and adequate reserves, not an assumed fixed yield.
families.coverageStatus: Extended USD universe identified. Ethena whole-product discovery value is not an ETH sleeve. Resolv has a documented historical failure/recovery case, but its current ETH collateral and eligible recovery value are unmeasured.

families.returnBasis: WBETH return is ETH conversion-ratio growth after reward commissions. Listed-fund investor total return includes share-price changes and distributions, less fund and staking costs; market discounts or premiums differ from NAV return.
families.exitTerms: WBETH redemption is quota- and queue-dependent and cannot be cancelled once requested. Retail ETF holders normally sell shares in the market; Authorized Participant creations/redemptions are a separate channel.

families.capacity: Exchange quotas, validator exit queues and custody/provider capacity. Fund market depth differs from underlying ETH redemption liquidity.
families.incentivesOff: Native staking earnings do not require promotions. WBETH Flexible Simple Earn does not add a second yield merely because it appears in another product menu. Fees can consume a substantial portion of gross staking return.
families.coverageStatus: Official exchange terms and historical public fund filing reviewed. Product-level current custodial assets and October policy amendments remain outside frozen-T reconstruction.
